paragraphs: Qualcomm Inc (QCOM) moved down by 3.26%. The Technology Equipment sector is down by 2.57%. The company underperformed the industry. Top 3 stocks by turnover in the sector: Micron Technology Inc (MU) down 5.80%; SanDisk Corporation (SNDK) down 9.98%; NVIDIA Corp (NVDA) down 2.46%.
What is driving Qualcomm Inc (QCOM)’s stock price down today?

The downward movement in Qualcomm's valuation today is primarily reflective of broader selling pressure within the semiconductor industry, triggered by shifting macroeconomic expectations. Investors appear to be rotating out of high-growth technology names as recent labor market data suggests a potential softening in consumer spending, raising concerns about the durability of the smartphone upgrade cycle. This macro backdrop is exacerbating profit-taking following a period of sustained performance in the artificial intelligence hardware space, impacting major players across the chip sector.

Specific industry dynamics are weighing on investor sentiment, particularly regarding the competitive landscape for 5G modems and AI-capable processors. Reports suggesting accelerated timelines for major handset manufacturers to transition toward in-house connectivity solutions are creating headwinds for the company's long-term licensing and chip supply revenue. Additionally, while the expansion into the PC market with ARM-based architecture has been a central growth narrative, recent channel checks indicate a more gradual adoption rate than some aggressive analyst forecasts had initially anticipated, leading to a recalibration of short-term revenue expectations.

Geopolitical tensions continue to cast a shadow over the semiconductor sector, with renewed discussions around export controls on advanced computing technology affecting firms with significant international exposure. As a company with a substantial footprint in global manufacturing and design hubs, any friction in cross-border trade or changes in international regulatory frameworks directly impacts its operational outlook. This regulatory uncertainty, combined with institutional portfolio adjustments ahead of the upcoming quarterly reporting cycle, has intensified the selling pressure observed during today's session.

Furthermore, a series of cautious notes from equity analysts has shifted the market's focus toward potential margin compression in the mobile handset segment. While the company remains a leader in edge computing and on-device AI, the high valuation multiples previously assigned to the stock are being tested by a more discerning investor base. The combination of cyclical headwinds in the core smartphone business and the execution risks associated with diversifying into automotive and industrial IoT sectors has prompted a defensive stance among institutional holders, contributing to the current volatility.

Technically, Qualcomm Inc (QCOM) shows a MACD (12,26,9) value of -2.481, indicating a sell signal. The RSI at 40.438 suggests neutral condition and the Williams %R at 87.614 suggests oversold condition. Please monitor closely.

Chinese Market Share Erosion: The resurgence of Huawei’s proprietary Kirin chipsets and increasing local-sourcing mandates in China create a direct threat to Qualcomm's dominant position in the high-end Android market, risking significant revenue contraction in its largest geographic segment.

Execution Risk in AI PC Transition: Despite the recent launch of the Snapdragon X Elite, intraday volatility is driven by concerns over x86 app emulation performance and the impending competitive response from Intel’s Lunar Lake architecture, which could limit Qualcomm’s penetration into the Windows PC market.

sourceContent.headline: Forecast: Consumer agentic AI will soar to $3.3tn in 2030
paragraphs: Forecast: Consumer agentic AI will soar to $3.3tn in 2030

Marketing is operating in an age of abundance. Today’s consumers face more content and choices than they have the attention or means to manage. AI agents are emerging as fundamental tools to help consumers cut through the noise and make decisions faster. Research by PHD in partnership with WARC reveals how quickly they are reshaping the customer journey.

The study finds that total agent-facilitated consumer spending will triple from $944 billion (€827.7bn) this year to $3.35 trillion in 2030. While consumers will still make most purchase decisions on their own in the next few years, AI agents will increasingly shape what gets seen, shortlisted and bought – and will increasingly mediate the boring, complex or repetitive tasks along the way.

As decision-making increasingly evolves from human consumers to machine intermediaries, this study explores the scale, timeline and implications for brands, agencies and the wider marketing ecosystem.

Rohan Tambyrajah, Worldwide Chief Strategy Officer at PHD, commented: “This research brings category level empiricism to the open-ended industry conversation about the growth opportunity with consumer facing AI and Agentic AI. It underscores the need for brands to design for both meaning and machine logic, and through Four Modes Framework offers marketers practical guidance on how best to implement against a category-level business case.”

James McDonald, Director of Data, Intelligence & Forecasting, WARC, and author of the research, added: “This landmark study finds that agentic AI is already facilitating the path to purchase for many consumers, and will become deeply embedded over the coming years to influence $3.35 trillion in household expenditure by 2030. This is true not just in high-frequency categories such as travel, CPG, and utilities, but increasingly more so in sectors that have traditionally leveraged brand marketing as a core strategy. By mapping adoption across product sectors, markets and media, our research ensures practitioners are not caught flat-footed as they approach the new frontier.”

The research draws on data provided by Acxiom and uses a weighted index approach to evaluate key factors such as decision complexity, transaction value, purchase frequency, data availability, media mix, and market regulation to make a holistic assessment of how much consumers will spend on AI channels in 2026 and 2030. The analysis covers the global viewpoint of ten markets: Australia, Brazil, China, France, Germany, India, Mexico, South Korea, UK and US. Additionally, it includes industry expert views and category analysis.
Categories and markets leading on agentic AI consumer spend

Agentic AI – artificial intelligence systems that understand goals, plans steps, and act autonomously – are making their mark on high-frequency categories like travel & transport, food, and media & publishing. By 2030, AI-facilitated spending will surge across all industries, especially where purchases are frequent and data-rich.

US: The US will lead agentic AI spending at $1.1 trillion (31.9 per cent of the global total), driven by consumers already comfortable with digital commerce and brands with the resources to deploy agents at scale.

China: China will be the second-largest market at $505.8 billion (15.1 per cent of global spend), powered by high platform integration, government support, and consumers ready to embrace delegated commerce.
UK: The UK will capture 3.9 per cent of global agentic AI spending ($131.2 billion), driven by strong talent, major investments, and government backing for AI-led transformation.

By mapping adoption across product sectors, markets and media, our research ensures practitioners are not caught flat-footed as they approach the new frontier.”

The research draws on data provided by Acxiom and uses a weighted index approach to evaluate key factors such as decision complexity, transaction value, purchase frequency, data availability, media mix, and market regulation to make a holistic assessment of how much consumers will spend on AI channels in 2026 and 2030. The analysis covers the global viewpoint of ten markets: Australia, Brazil, China, France, Germany, India, Mexico, South Korea, UK and US. Additionally, it includes industry expert views and category analysis.

Categories and markets leading on agentic AI consumer spend

Agentic AI – artificial intelligence systems that understand goals, plans steps, and act autonomously – are making their mark on high-frequency categories like travel & transport, food, and media & publishing. By 2030, AI-facilitated spending will surge across all industries, especially where purchases are frequent and data-rich.

US: The US will lead agentic AI spending at $1.1 trillion (31.9 per cent of the global total), driven by consumers already comfortable with digital commerce and brands with the resources to deploy agents at scale.

China: China will be the second-largest market at $505.8 billion (15.1 per cent of global spend), powered by high platform integration, government support, and consumers ready to embrace delegated commerce.

UK: The UK will capture 3.9 per cent of global agentic AI spending ($131.2 billion), driven by strong talent, major investments, and government backing for AI-led transformation.

How agentic AI will affect consumer spending: introducing The Four Modes Framework

Agent adoption will surge where purchases are repetitive, searchable, and measurable—not necessarily high-volume or low-value, just routine enough for AI to own the entire journey.

The three industry categories where agentic AI will have the greatest impact are:

1. Telecoms & Utilities will grow 611.9 per cent from $57.6 billion in 2026 to $410.3 billion by 2030 – making it the largest category for AI agents. Information-dense, frequent billing, and comparison-led contract switching make these infrequent but high-value purchases ideal for AI delegation.

2. Financial Services decisions are too sensitive to fully delegate, but too complex not to be agent-assisted. Total agent-facilitated consumer spending will increase 235.3 per cent to $237.9 billion by 2030.

3. Travel & Transport will lead agent-facilitated spending at $78.1 billion in 2026, surging 252.8 per cent to $275.6 billion by 2030 as AI agents take control of discovery, planning, and booking.

sourceContent.headline: 71% young Indians use AI for career advice
sourceContent.description: PulseAI Research, Smytten's consumer insights division, surveyed over 2,000 Indians for The AI Companion Report on how AI is shaping learning, work and decisions.
paragraphs: PulseAI Research, Smytten's consumer insights division, surveyed over 2,000 Indians for The AI Companion Report on how AI is shaping learning, work and decisions.

New Delhi: A majority of young Indians are using artificial intelligence (AI) beyond work and productivity, with over 70% seeking career advice from AI tools and nearly half saying their daily lives would be disrupted if they lost access to AI for a week, according to a study by PulseAI Research, the consumer insights division of Smytten.

The report, titled 'The AI Companion Report: How Young Indians Are Learning, Working, and Making Decisions with AI', surveyed more than 2,000 respondents across India, most of them aged between 18 and 34 years.

According to the study, 70.6% of respondents have already used AI for career advice, while 62% said they would be comfortable using it for career coaching in the future. More than half also said they would consider AI for health guidance, travel planning, fitness advice and financial planning.

The report found that 41.4% of respondents now turn to AI before using search engines when looking for information online. Nearly 65% said AI has reduced the time they spend searching for information, while 47% said their daily lives would be moderately or significantly disrupted if AI became unavailable for just one week.

Learning emerged as the biggest use case for AI, with 29.8% of respondents saying they primarily use it for studying and learning, followed by research and information gathering (22.3%). Research (29.6%) and creative ideation (29.4%) were the most commonly delegated tasks.

Despite the growing adoption, respondents highlighted concerns around AI. Overdependence on technology (27.8%) and privacy (27.6%) emerged as the top issues, followed by concerns over inaccurate information (16.9%).

Commenting on the findings, Swagata Sarangi, Co-founder of PulseAI Research, said: “AI isn't replacing human judgment; it's fundamentally changing how judgment is formed. For decades, enterprise decisions have relied on probabilistic predictions drawn from historical data. The next frontier is deterministic future intelligence, AI that continuously learns from real consumer behaviour, validates every signal, and enables businesses to act with far greater confidence about what comes next.

The companies that win won't simply have more data; they'll have better intelligence. At PulseAI Research, we're building AI that transforms billions of consumer signals into validated, decision-ready intelligence, enabling brands to act with greater confidence instead of navigating a maze of disconnected predictive models.”

PulseAI Research said the study was conducted among 2,000 consumers across India, with 88.2% of respondents belonging to the 18-34 age group, to understand changing perceptions, usage patterns and trust in AI.

sourceContent.description: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) cleared for China AI launch as iPhone sales test 24% jump - TechStock²
paragraphs: China approved Apple Intelligence following early numbers showing Apple’s mainland shipments up 24.4% in Q2, as the overall market slipped 4.3%.
Apple hit a new high of $325.65, then traded at $324.03. That puts Apple’s market cap at $4.77 trillion, 39.2 times its trailing earnings.

Apple Inc. NASDAQ:AAPL got regulatory clearance for its Apple Intelligence product in China on Wednesday, moving the focus for investors to the staying power of Apple’s recent rebound in the country. The rally started before Apple Intelligence launched. IDC’s estimates, rounded, show Apple shipped about 2.4 million more iPhones year-on-year in mainland China in the June quarter.

The point is, the stock is set up for another move. Apple was up 2.9% to $324.03 late in the morning, hitting a new intraday high and tacking on roughly $135 billion in market cap. The Nasdaq Composite edged up 0.24%.

China’s cyberspace regulator said Apple Intelligence was one of seven phone-based generative AI services to finish registration, which is needed before they can launch to the public. The notice did not say when Apple Intelligence might be released in China. Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. NYSE:BABA said its Qwen AI model is set to work with Apple’s iPhone, iPad, Mac and Vision Pro devices in China. Baidu Inc. NASDAQ:BIDU said it is also working with Apple to bring features to Chinese iPhone users. On-device AI keeps some processing on the phone itself.
Early IDC numbers point to a stark divide between Apple and the rest of the market:

Applying Apple’s share to IDC’s 66 million-unit estimate, Apple moved about 11.9 million phones, up from 9.6 million in the same period last year. It’s an increase, but not enough to confirm a new AI-fueled device replacement wave. “Huawei and Apple held their prices steady while competitors were raising theirs,” said IDC analyst Arthur Guo. IDC said some promotions and talk of second-half Apple price hikes also pushed buyers to act early. IDC

Apple’s Greater China business was already picking up before this week’s registration. Net sales in the region climbed 28% to $20.5 billion in the March quarter, making up 18.4% of its total revenue. Apple credited most of the gain to iPhone. The shipment and revenue numbers track different timeframes and areas, but both suggest the recovery started before any local Apple Intelligence launch.

Wall Street is split on whether Apple can keep up its strength with higher prices. KeyBanc Capital Markets’ Brandon Nispel downgraded Apple to Underweight, set a $250 target, and pointed to slower device upgrades. He sees Services growing 7% in fiscal 2027, well below the nearly 12% the market is pricing in. But Morgan Stanley NYSE:MS analyst Erik Woodring stuck with his Overweight call and $360 target, saying product price hikes could add 2% to 4% to fiscal Q3 EPS and about 1% to fiscal 2027 EPS.

Investors see a simple story here. Getting China approval lifts the bull case, but that doesn’t mean new revenue right away. Apple has to use this to drive more upgrades, hold on to customers longer or push up Services. The stock trades at 39.2 times trailing earnings, so there’s not much room for delays, a weak rollout or no bump in replacement rates.

Clearance isn’t a launch. Apple still needs to rely on local AI models, and there’s no timeline from regulators. IDC is warning China’s market drop might hit 20% in the second half if things stay as they are. CEO Tim Cook has said “memory costs will drive an increasing impact on our business.” Higher prices could help margins but risk cooling the buying that fueled Apple’s June quarter. Reuters

Apple’s July 30 fiscal Q3 report is next up. Investors are focused on Greater China sales, product margins, and any launch updates. Another quarter of share gains after recent price hikes would back Woodring, while weaker results from pulled-forward demand would help Nispel. Beijing lifted restrictions, but the valuation debate is ongoing.

paragraphs: The global cloud kitchen market was valued at USD 81.94 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 248.10 billion by 2035, expanding at a CAGR of 11.72% from 2026 to 2035. Growth is driven by rising demand for online food delivery, busy urban lifestyles, increasing smartphone and internet penetration, and the rapid adoption of AI-powered kitchen management, automation, and delivery technologies. The expansion of shared kitchens, digital ordering platforms, and delivery-first business models is further creating significant growth opportunities across the global food service industry.
Why is the Cloud Kitchen Market Growing So Rapidly Worldwide?

The global cloud kitchen market size is accounted at USD 81.94 billion in 2025 and predicted to increase from USD 91.70 billion in 2026 to approximately USD 248.10 billion by 2035, representing a CAGR of 11.72% from 2026 to 2035. The global cloud kitchen market growth is attributed to the increasing preference for convenient dining options, the increasing busy lifestyles and urbanization, and the rise of food delivery apps.
North America is expected to grow at the fastest CAGR between 2026 and 2035.
By type, the independent cloud kitchen segment generated the biggest market share in 2025.
By type, the commissary/shared kitchen segment is expanding at the fastest CAGR between 2026 and 2035.
By nature of operation, the single-brand segment accounted for the largest market share in 2025.
By nature of operation, the hybrid model segment is projected to grow at a solid CAGR between 2026 and 2035.
By cuisine type, the ethnic cuisine segment captured the highest market share in 2025.
By cuisine type, the health-conscious and organic food segment is poised to grow at a healthy CAGR between 2026 and 2035.
By order source, the online food aggregators segment contributed the highest market share in 2025.
By order source, the restaurant-owned platforms and websites segment is growing at a strong CAGR between 2026 and 2035.
By technology platform, the order and delivery management software segment held a major market share in 2025.
By technology platform, the AI, robotics, and automation segment is expected to expand at a notable CAGR from 2026 to 2035.
By end-user, the startups and small enterprises segment held a major market share in 2025.
By end-user, the delivery aggregators segment is expected to expand at a notable CAGR from 2026 to 2035.

A cloud kitchen is a delivery-only food preparation facility that does not have a dine-in area or storefront staff. These kitchens rely solely on online food delivery apps and direct-to-consumer websites to process orders. This model maximizes profitability by reducing the high costs associated with prime real estate and traditional dining operations. The market is driven by rapid urbanization, increasing smartphone usage, and a booming online food delivery sector. A structural shift in consumer habits, along with the expansion of food delivery platforms, makes this model highly appealing for food entrepreneurs with minimal upfront capital.

Artificial Intelligence has become an essential part of our technology in recent years. Artificial Intelligence plays a very important role, from controlling the apps to every device. AI-generated robots can cook customer's favorite food delivered to their doorstep. The installation cost of AI is cost-effective and does not need any manpower. Orders can be accepted by voice commands, with the help of Artificial Intelligence. Customers can easily receive the same treatment as restaurants through their devices and prevent long lines to place their orders at restaurants. The number of daily sales is estimated to go up with less investment in human labor fancy infrastructure, with the installment of Artificial Intelligence. AI-generated restaurants do not require hiring people to track, take orders, cook, and deliver orders. All one needs is an AI assistant to handle all functions. Due to these advanced and convenient AI trends, AI will take food apps and other businesses to a higher level and further revolutionize the growth of the cloud kitchen market.

By order source, the restaurant-owned platforms and websites segment is growing at a strong CAGR between 2026 and 2035.

By technology platform, the order and delivery management software segment held a major market share in 2025.

By technology platform, the AI, robotics, and automation segment is expected to expand at a notable CAGR from 2026 to 2035.

By end-user, the startups and small enterprises segment held a major market share in 2025.

By end-user, the delivery aggregators segment is expected to expand at a notable CAGR from 2026 to 2035.

A cloud kitchen is a delivery-only food preparation facility that does not have a dine-in area or storefront staff. These kitchens rely solely on online food delivery apps and direct-to-consumer websites to process orders. This model maximizes profitability by reducing the high costs associated with prime real estate and traditional dining operations. The market is driven by rapid urbanization, increasing smartphone usage, and a booming online food delivery sector. A structural shift in consumer habits, along with the expansion of food delivery platforms, makes this model highly appealing for food entrepreneurs with minimal upfront capital.

Artificial Intelligence has become an essential part of our technology in recent years. Artificial Intelligence plays a very important role, from controlling the apps to every device. AI-generated robots can cook customer's favorite food delivered to their doorstep. The installation cost of AI is cost-effective and does not need any manpower. Orders can be accepted by voice commands, with the help of Artificial Intelligence. Customers can easily receive the same treatment as restaurants through their devices and prevent long lines to place their orders at restaurants. The number of daily sales is estimated to go up with less investment in human labor fancy infrastructure, with the installment of Artificial Intelligence. AI-generated restaurants do not require hiring people to track, take orders, cook, and deliver orders. All one needs is an AI assistant to handle all functions. Due to these advanced and convenient AI trends, AI will take food apps and other businesses to a higher level and further revolutionize the growth of the cloud kitchen market.

The growing demand for food coupled with the rising global population, rising disposable income, increased demand for conveniences, and proliferation of digital technologies are the major factors that drive the global cloud kitchen market.

The rising preferences for online food delivery over the dine-in experience and the rapid growth and penetration of the various online food delivery apps such as Zomato, Swiggy, EatSure, and Grubhub have exponentially supported the growth of the global cloud kitchen market.

The ease of doing business and favorable government policies regarding food delivery and kitchens have made it easier to start a cloud kitchen. There are various organizations that train and guide people to start their own cloud kitchens. This has boosted the number of small and independent cloud kitchens, especially in developing countries.

The increased penetration of the internet, growing adoption of smartphones, and adequate support from food delivery platforms have contributed to the growth of the cloud kitchen market.

The increasing demand for online food delivery services has forced restaurateurs to start cloud kitchen outlets in order to serve online customers. The increasing penetration of social media and the digital marketing strategies adopted by the top market players is significantly contributing to the market growth.

The doorstep delivery of food and the availability of 24/7 customer care support are boosting the adoption of food delivery apps among global customers. Cloud kitchens are gaining popularity as operating costs are lower and the profit margins are higher compared to those of the restaurants. Further, flexibility in operations is another major factor that has supplemented the growth of the cloud kitchen across the globe.

Industry Growth Overview : The cloud kitchen will experience high growth between 2025 and 2030 as a continued increase in online food delivery drives expansion with low operating costs. The growth of delivery platforms and changing consumer behavior in the Asia-Pacific and North America will support stronger expansion rates for niche cuisines and premium meals.

Sustainable Practices Trends: Cloud kitchens adopt eco-friendly packaging, energy-efficient appliances, and waste-reducing systems. Brands such as Rebel Foods and Kitopi are incorporating sustainable sourcing and AI-powered inventory control to reduce food waste and ensure they are able to align operations with sustainability goals globally, while meeting consumers' expectations for greener food delivery.

Global Expansion: Leading brands are expanding into emerging regions, including Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and LATAM, to capture growing online consumers. Partnerships with delivery aggregators and real estate developers are facilitating faster setups and scales with high-demand urban cores.

Key Investors : Venture capital and private equity firms are firmly invested in scalable, technology-driven kitchen concepts. These big investors have invested in delivery-first brands and more complex infrastructure startups for high-margin returns in the digital food system.

Startup Ecosystem : The startup ecosystem has a vibrant community of players developing automation, virtual branding, and AI-driven optimization of menus. CloudEats in the Philippines and Karma Kitchen in the UK are good examples of developing traction with shared kitchen space and data-led culinary development.

The cloud kitchen model is revolutionizing the food service industry by minimizing front-of-house real estate costs, allowing operators to focus exclusively on food preparation and delivery. Government initiatives aimed at expanding digital infrastructure have accelerated this delivery-first strategy, enabling businesses to optimize kitchen space, scale efficiently, and lower operating expenses compared to traditional dine-in restaurants.

Despite its potential, the market faces challenges due to oversaturation and a heavy reliance on third-party food delivery platforms. Operators struggle with high customer acquisition costs while competing for visibility within aggregator apps. Low entry barriers have led to identical virtual brands flooding the market, creating fierce competition. Furthermore, stringent safety compliance mandates pose regulatory challenges that all virtual food hubs must navigate to operate legally.

The market is poised for significant opportunities to reach previously untapped consumer bases. Government-backed digital commerce initiatives, such as the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC), greatly reduce entry barriers, lower customer acquisition costs, and enable independent kitchens to compete fairly against larger chains. Additionally, leveraging data analytics and AI for dynamic menu pricing and demand forecasting helps maximize profitability in different regions.

sourceContent.headline: Intel Q2 2026 Revenue Surges 25% as AI Server Chips, Foundry Business and PC Demand Fuel Strongest Growth in 15 Years - InfotechLead
sourceContent.description: Intel delivered its strongest quarterly revenue growth during the second quarter of 2026, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure
paragraphs: Intel delivered its strongest quarterly revenue growth in more than 15 years during the second quarter of 2026, driven by surging demand for AI infrastructure, data center processors, premium PC chips and expanding foundry services.

The semiconductor giant exceeded its financial guidance, raised its capital investment plans and issued a stronger-than-expected outlook for the third quarter as enterprise AI deployments continued to accelerate.
Intel reported Q2 2026 revenue of $16.1 billion, an increase of 25 percent, significantly above its guidance range of $14.4 billion to $15.4 billion.

Intel’s Data Center and AI (DCAI) business emerged as the biggest growth driver. Revenue surged 59 percent to $6.3 billion, supported by adoption of Xeon 6 processors, increasing AI server deployments and rising demand for CPUs powering agentic AI workloads. The company said CPU demand is now outpacing supply as enterprises continue expanding AI infrastructure.

Intel’s Client Computing and Physical AI Group (CCPG) delivered $6.3 billion in revenue with 13 percent increase as demand shifted toward premium AI-enabled PCs. Intel continued focusing on higher-value processors, helping improve average selling prices despite lower overall PC unit volumes. Management said commercial PC refresh cycles and AI PC adoption are supporting stronger profitability across the client business.

The latest Omdia report said PC refresh cycles are slowing as rising component costs force businesses to delay upgrades, even as AI PC adoption gains momentum. Omdia said more than half of B2B channel partners reported customers postponing hardware refresh plans until market conditions stabilize, while 6 percent expect outright cancellations. Enterprises are considering AI-capable PCs to support local AI workloads and improve productivity. However, higher memory, storage and device prices could limit adoption, extending replacement cycles and weakening second-half 2026 PC demand.

Intel Foundry generated $5.8 billion in revenue, representing 31 percent growth. The foundry business benefited from increasing external customer engagements, including new manufacturing agreements, while Intel reaffirmed its commitment to its advanced 14A manufacturing process, which it expects to become highly competitive by 2028. The company highlighted growing long-term customer commitments for advanced manufacturing services.

Reflecting confidence in future demand, Intel increased its planned 2026 capital expenditure to $20 billion, up from earlier expectations, to expand manufacturing capacity and meet rising AI-driven processor demand.

The company ended the quarter with approximately $30 billion in cash and investments, supported by an additional $10 billion credit facility that provides financial flexibility for manufacturing expansion and technology investments.

Looking ahead, Intel forecast third-quarter 2026 revenue between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion. Intel said continued momentum in AI servers, enterprise computing, foundry services and premium PCs is expected to sustain growth through the second half of 2026.

sourceContent.headline: Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini: Lead Slips to 58%
sourceContent.description: Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini: ChatGPT is still primary for 58% of US users while Gemini takes 25%. See who wins each task before you pick a tool.
paragraphs: In the Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini race, ChatGPT is still the primary assistant for 58% of US users, but Gemini has climbed to 25%.

The Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini contest is reshaping the consumer AI assistant market, as Google Gemini and Anthropic’s Claude rapidly expand their user bases and narrow ChatGPT’s once-dominant lead. While ChatGPT remains the world’s most widely used AI assistant, recent market data indicates its share of primary AI assistant users has declined as rivals gain traction through tighter ecosystem integration, enterprise adoption, and specialized capabilities.

The changing competitive landscape reflects the maturation of the generative AI industry. Rather than relying on a single chatbot, users are increasingly choosing different AI assistants based on specific tasks such as coding, research, productivity, or integration with existing software. This shift has intensified competition among leading AI companies, including OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Microsoft, and Meta.
A recent survey of U.S. AI assistant users found that ChatGPT remains the primary AI assistant for 58% of users , maintaining a clear lead over competitors.
Anthropic Claude: Smaller overall share but strong adoption among technical users.
Other assistants, including Meta AI and Microsoft’s Copilot, continue expanding their user bases.
Google has rapidly expanded Gemini by integrating it across its ecosystem, including:

This built-in distribution has significantly increased Gemini’s adoption without materially reducing Google’s traditional search traffic. Recent market data also shows Gemini’s web traffic and mobile usage have grown sharply over the past year, and Gemini has already overtaken ChatGPT in Instagram creator conversations . Google is also working on cheaper serving infrastructure, including a new AI chip codenamed “Frozen v2” aimed at running Gemini models far more efficiently .
Anthropic’s Claude has emerged as one of the preferred AI assistants for technical and enterprise users.

Research suggests Claude captures a disproportionately large share of coding-related tasks despite having a smaller overall market share, highlighting its strength in specialized professional workflows. Anthropic has been steadily hardening the product for that audience — it recently began testing a new Projects sidebar for Claude Desktop to make long-running work easier to organise.
Instead of one AI assistant dominating every use case, users are increasingly selecting different models for different tasks.
ChatGPT for general-purpose conversations and creativity.
This growing specialization suggests the AI assistant market is evolving toward a multi-platform ecosystem rather than a winner-takes-all environment.

Although ChatGPT’s relative share has declined as competitors expand, it continues to hold the largest overall user base and remains one of the most recognized AI brands globally. At the same time, Google and Anthropic are leveraging their respective strengths — ecosystem integration and enterprise-focused capabilities — to attract new users and diversify the market.

The increased competition is also accelerating innovation, with leading AI companies introducing more capable reasoning models, multimodal features, AI agents, and deeper integrations into everyday software platforms.

The AI assistant market is entering a new phase where growth is being driven not only by model quality but also by ecosystem reach, enterprise adoption, and specialized use cases. While ChatGPT continues to lead in overall usage, Google’s Gemini is rapidly expanding through its integration across Search, Android, and Workspace, while Anthropic’s Claude has established a strong position among developers and enterprise customers.

Rather than signaling the decline of any single platform, the latest trends point to a more competitive and diversified AI ecosystem. As companies continue investing in reasoning capabilities, AI agents, and productivity tools, users are likely to benefit from faster innovation and greater choice, with different assistants increasingly optimized for different tasks instead of competing solely on overall market share.

There is no single winner. ChatGPT leads on overall usage and general-purpose conversation, Gemini wins on Google ecosystem integration across Search, Android, and Workspace, and Claude is favoured for coding and long-document analysis. The survey cited here measures which assistant people use most, not which model is objectively best.

paragraphs: The global polypropylene market was valued at USD 193.91 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 293.54 billion by 2035, growing at a CAGR of 14.35% from 2026 to 2035. Market growth is driven by increasing demand for lightweight, durable, and recyclable materials across the packaging, automotive, healthcare, construction, and consumer goods industries. Strategic Recommendations for Stakeholders: Stakeholders can drive sustainable growth by investing in circular infrastructure and localized collection networks to secure raw materials. To ensure seamless operations and avoid market friction, stakeholders should monitor updates for polypropylene materials to avoid distribution restrictions. Furthermore, companies should leverage subsidies in government-sponsored Petrochemical and Plastic Parks and prioritize research and development of light weighting to enhance fuel efficiency and comply with emission targets.

Increasing demand for sustainable and lightweight packaging materials across the food and e-commerce industries is expected to drive the market. Its strong position in flexible and rigid packaging is extended with continuous innovation of barrier films made from materials that can be recycled, and the development of packaging innovations. Furthermore, the rising sustainability regulations, expanding packaged food production, and increasing investments in recyclable plastic packaging are projected to sustain long-term demand across global packaging industries.

Furthermore, expanding environmental regulations and sustainability requirements are likely to limit conventional polypropylene consumption in selected applications.

MSA Safety's acquisition of M&Cor TechGroup is helping to shape the industrial gas analysis market's competitive landscape.
As a result of Breath Diagnostics' breakthrough February 2026 FDA designation, regulatory credibility in the breath-diagnostics segment is moving forward at a rapid pace.
We are seeing more use of automated compliance across food-packaging QS following Bizerba's automation solution, LeakSecure, launch at Empack 2026.
Ainos' growth and robotics investments now provide a wider roadmap for commercialization possibilities in the smart-sensing segment of the electronics industry.

The rise of complex odor signatures and artificial intelligence is changing the way companies utilize electronic nose systems to detect, classify, and respond. In 2026, robot olfaction progress was summarized in a review article in npj Robotics. This outlines the vast progress of digital noses towards increased sensitivity and improved localization of odor sources. This improvement helps with search and rescue operations and quicker identification of gas leaks. These systems are now based on four major types of sensors. Including metal oxide, electrochemical, optical, and field-effect transistors, each with its characteristic advantages and drawbacks.

The miniaturisation of sensors is also moving at a fast pace. In September 2024, the UNIST team developed an ultra-small electronic nose. It can precisely detect and measure the type and concentration of gas. The small device components will reduce the cost of the device and improve its portability for use in mobile diagnostic solutions. The push to move forward continues with healthcare diagnostics. Requireing ultra compact, low-power sensor array structures that are suitable for clinical and even wearable environments. The food quality monitoring process is more or less comparable. Manufacturers want real-time alerts about contamination, instead of waiting for laboratory testing. Furthermore, the collective efforts are bringing e-nose systems out of the research laboratory and into a wide array of practical applications.

The change at the materials level began to manifest itself in mid-2026. Researchers came up with a plan for a so-called artificial olfactory system. Under the guidance of Hyuk-Jun Kwon, a researcher at Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Technology (DGIST). The team systematically investigated the research trends of design methods for metal-organic framework materials, realization of sensors using MOFs, and AI-based odor pattern recognition using MOFs. This roadmap represents a trend towards e-noses capable of distinguishing many more odors. Than previous generations, which were based on metal oxides alone. These days, range is learning to compete with speed.

On the other hand, long-standing companies such as MSA Safety, Owlstone Medical, SICK, Endress+Hauser and Sensirion are pushing on with commercial roll-outs in safety, healthcare, and process applications. The eNose Company has also expanded its clinical uses. Making the company more prominent in the field of medical diagnostics using breath. This combination of AI-powered pattern recognition, new sensing materials, and miniature equipment is moving e-nose use beyond its traditional industrial applications. They will likely shape the construction of the next generation of diagnostic and environmental monitoring devices through 2035.

This trend continued throughout 2025, as the E-Nose market's global value hit USD 426 million. They also note that analysts estimate a strong market will be realized by 2035, growing at a compound annual rate of 28.06% through the decade. Volume growth is parallel, as shipping volumes increase while the per-unit sensor costs continue to decrease. As a result of improvements in metal-oxide and MEMS manufacturing. Manufacturing prices remain in retreat, as chipmakers turn to an increasingly smaller sensor array for making semiconductors. Sales prices for clinical grade breath analyzers have yet to become competitive with industrial gas-monitoring units. Even a high-tech e-nose can cost over USD 50,000, a price too steep for smaller enterprises and consumers.

Metal-oxide semiconductor (MOS) sensors continue to be the technology of choice in the majority of food safety and industrial applications. Because of their high sensitivity and low production expense. The field-effect transistor and optical sensor type is showing the greatest growth. Driven in part by the need for smaller, wearable devices needed for diagnostics in health care. Exhaled breath analysis is an emerging, convenient, portable, safe diagnostic technique with high interest at the moment. On the other hand, Asia-Pacific is proving to be the most dynamic area with dense research output from institutions all over South Korea, China, and India region. This is paving the way for a wave of strategic developments to be analyzed in the coming years.

The introduction of artificial intelligence (AI) representation is at the heart of almost every strategic move to be seen during the e-nose development in 2026. The Daegu Gyeongbuk Institute of Technology researcher Hyuk-Jun Kwon has identified a roadmap. Integrating metal-organic framework with AI based on odor pattern recognition in a paper published in Progress in Materials Science. It's the combination of a novel sensing material and machine learning. This enables modern e-noses to identify larger odor libraries than those older single-sensor designs would have been able to in the past. The technology is expected to be adopted fastest in healthcare. Because diagnostic accuracy is strongly related to the ability of algorithms to interpret the noisy, real-world breath.

The technology of sensing is at the core of these individual breakthroughs. This is being connected to the Internet through IoT to form deployable networks. On the future outlook, the best investment opportunities are still in these projects that are being translated from the laboratory to the point-of-care. Laboratory prototypes of sensors are being developed into devices ready for use in both the clinic and industry. This will continue to influence funding priorities throughout the decade and beyond.

paragraphs: The global De-identified Health Data Market is expected to witness significant expansion as healthcare organizations, life sciences companies, and technology providers increasingly rely on privacy-compliant healthcare data to accelerate innovation while safeguarding patient confidentiality. “According to a recent study by SNS Insider, the global De-identified Health Data Market size valued at USD 8.52 billion in 2025, is anticipated to grow to USD 20.79 billion by 2035, registering a CAGR of 9.32% over the 2026–2035 forecast period.”

However, with the increasing volume of clinical data from healthcare institutions across the globe using digital healthcare platforms, EMR, laboratory databases, and connected healthcare technology, there is an increase in the need for innovation within healthcare that is leading institutions to embrace de-identified data which facilitates medical research, artificial intelligence innovation, healthcare planning, and pharmaceutical innovation.

As healthcare continues its digital transformation, secure data-sharing practices are becoming increasingly important for supporting scientific discovery, improving healthcare delivery, and advancing evidence-based medicine.

AI and Real-World Data Continue to Transform Healthcare Research

Artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and machine learning are being increasingly adopted in healthcare to enhance diagnostics, streamline treatment algorithms, and aid clinical decision making. For this purpose, access to varied and high-quality data sets that preserve patient confidentiality is essential.

De-identified health data is emerging as an important asset for pharmaceutical firms, biotech companies, academia, and innovators in digital health to advance their research and development efforts. Developments in cloud computing and other privacy-preserving technologies have made de-identified health data more accessible for research purposes.

Growing collaboration among healthcare providers, technology companies, and research organizations is expected to create new opportunities for responsible data utilization while strengthening compliance with evolving privacy regulations.

By data category, clinical data accounted for approximately 20.6% of global market revenue in 2025, reflecting its central role in medical research, healthcare analytics , and evidence generation. Meanwhile, behavioral and patient-reported data is projected to record the fastest growth through 2035, driven by increasing adoption of digital health platforms, wearable technologies, and patient engagement solutions.

Across applications, clinical research and trials represented approximately 25.62% of total market revenue in 2025, supported by growing reliance on real-world health information to improve study design and accelerate research activities. However, drug discovery and development is expected to emerge as the fastest-growing application segment, fueled by expanding use of AI-driven drug development and precision medicine initiatives.

Among end users, healthcare providers generated the largest market revenue in 2025, reflecting their role as major producers and users of clinical information. At the same time, pharmaceutical companies are anticipated to register the fastest growth during the forecast period, supported by increasing investments in real-world evidence, biomarker research, and advanced therapeutic development.
Privacy Technologies and Digital Health Infrastructure Drive Market Evolution

Healthcare organizations are focusing on deploying technology solutions that ensure proper handling of data while complying with changing regulations. The use of advanced privacy solutions and secure data exchange solutions, together with advanced analytics, is assisting organizations in extracting the maximum possible benefit from healthcare data while ensuring patient privacy.

The expansion of precision medicine, value-based healthcare, and population health initiatives is also creating new opportunities for organizations capable of delivering reliable, privacy-compliant healthcare datasets that support large-scale research and clinical innovation.

The North American market had 39.7% of the world market revenue in 2025 due to its sophisticated digitization of healthcare, high usage of electronic health records , regulatory frameworks, and investments made in healthcare analytics and life sciences research. North America continues to be a world leader in building healthcare data ecosystem that complies with privacy standards.

On the other hand, the Asia-Pacific region will become the world's most rapidly growing market until 2035 due to its rapid healthcare digitization, development of electronic health systems, biotech investments, and government initiatives to modernize healthcare data.
Leading Companies Focus on Data Innovation and Strategic Partnerships

Competition within the de-identified health data market continues to intensify as organizations invest in advanced analytics, secure data platforms, interoperability solutions, and AI-enabled healthcare intelligence. Strategic collaborations between healthcare providers, technology companies, and pharmaceutical organizations are further strengthening innovation across the industry.

As healthcare continues its digital transformation, secure data-sharing practices are becoming increasingly important for supporting scientific discovery, improving healthcare delivery, and advancing evidence-based medicine.

AI and Real-World Data Continue to Transform Healthcare Research

Artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, and machine learning are being increasingly adopted in healthcare to enhance diagnostics, streamline treatment algorithms, and aid clinical decision making. For this purpose, access to varied and high-quality data sets that preserve patient confidentiality is essential.

De-identified health data is emerging as an important asset for pharmaceutical firms, biotech companies, academia, and innovators in digital health to advance their research and development efforts. Developments in cloud computing and other privacy-preserving technologies have made de-identified health data more accessible for research purposes.

Growing collaboration among healthcare providers, technology companies, and research organizations is expected to create new opportunities for responsible data utilization while strengthening compliance with evolving privacy regulations.

By data category, clinical data accounted for approximately 20.6% of global market revenue in 2025, reflecting its central role in medical research, healthcare analytics , and evidence generation. Meanwhile, behavioral and patient-reported data is projected to record the fastest growth through 2035, driven by increasing adoption of digital health platforms, wearable technologies, and patient engagement solutions.

Across applications, clinical research and trials represented approximately 25.62% of total market revenue in 2025, supported by growing reliance on real-world health information to improve study design and accelerate research activities. However, drug discovery and development is expected to emerge as the fastest-growing application segment, fueled by expanding use of AI-driven drug development and precision medicine initiatives.

Among end users, healthcare providers generated the largest market revenue in 2025, reflecting their role as major producers and users of clinical information. At the same time, pharmaceutical companies are anticipated to register the fastest growth during the forecast period, supported by increasing investments in real-world evidence, biomarker research, and advanced therapeutic development.

Privacy Technologies and Digital Health Infrastructure Drive Market Evolution

Healthcare organizations are focusing on deploying technology solutions that ensure proper handling of data while complying with changing regulations. The use of advanced privacy solutions and secure data exchange solutions, together with advanced analytics, is assisting organizations in extracting the maximum possible benefit from healthcare data while ensuring patient privacy.

The expansion of precision medicine, value-based healthcare, and population health initiatives is also creating new opportunities for organizations capable of delivering reliable, privacy-compliant healthcare datasets that support large-scale research and clinical innovation.

The North American market had 39.7% of the world market revenue in 2025 due to its sophisticated digitization of healthcare, high usage of electronic health records , regulatory frameworks, and investments made in healthcare analytics and life sciences research. North America continues to be a world leader in building healthcare data ecosystem that complies with privacy standards.

On the other hand, the Asia-Pacific region will become the world's most rapidly growing market until 2035 due to its rapid healthcare digitization, development of electronic health systems, biotech investments, and government initiatives to modernize healthcare data.

Leading Companies Focus on Data Innovation and Strategic Partnerships

Competition within the de-identified health data market continues to intensify as organizations invest in advanced analytics, secure data platforms, interoperability solutions, and AI-enabled healthcare intelligence. Strategic collaborations between healthcare providers, technology companies, and pharmaceutical organizations are further strengthening innovation across the industry.

Key companies operating in the global de-identified health data market include IQVIA, Oracle Health, Merative, Optum, Veradigm, HealthVerity, Truveta, Komodo Health, Tempus, and Datavant.

According to MarketsandMarkets™, the Application Security market size was valued at USD 12.19 billion in 2025 and is projected to grow from USD 13.6 billion in 2026 to USD 23.45 billion by 2031, exhibiting a CAGR of 11.5% during the forecast period. The fast rise of cloud-native applications, microservices architectures, and API-driven development is driving market growth, resulting in a greatly increased attack surface across current software systems. As enterprises accelerate digital transformation and deploy apps more frequently via CI/CD pipelines, security flaws are usually introduced earlier in the development cycle. This is creating a high need for integrated application security solutions that automate vulnerability detection, secure coding techniques, and continuous testing across the software development life cycle (SDLC) to avoid exploitation before deployment.
Download PDF Brochure@ https://www.marketsandmarkets.com/pdfdownloadNew.asp?id=110170194

Rising adoption of DevSecOps and agile software development practices is a key driving factor for the application security market. As organizations accelerate application delivery, integrating security early in the development lifecycle has become essential to prevent costly breaches and compliance issues. Continuous integration and deployment pipelines require automated security testing, vulnerability scanning, and code analysis to ensure secure releases. This shift toward “security as code” is boosting demand for comprehensive application security solutions that can seamlessly support rapid development cycles while maintaining robust protection.
By security testing tools, IAST to register the highest CAGR during the forecast period.

Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST) equips developers with comprehensive contextual data, encompassing vulnerable code locations, potential exploit pathways, and remediation strategies, while significantly mitigating false positive occurrences. Its integration with automated testing frameworks facilitates continuous security validation without necessitating separate security scans. IAST demonstrates particular efficacy for contemporary web applications, application programming interfaces (APIs), microservices, and cloud-native architectures, where insight into runtime behavior is imperative. As organizations strive for expedited vulnerability identification with minimal disruption to software delivery, IAST is experiencing increased adoption as a complementary technology that enhances testing efficiency, accelerates remediation efforts, and fortifies overall application security within agile development environments.
By deployment mode, cloud segment to register highest CAGR during forecast period.

The cloud-based deployment segment is expected to register a higher CAGR than the on-premises segment during the forecast period. The shift toward digital transformation and the growing reliance on cloud ecosystems are driving the rapid adoption of cloud-based application security. With enterprises increasingly deploying SaaS platforms, cloud-native applications, and supporting remote workforce operations, scalable and flexible security solutions have become essential. Cloud-based application security provides benefits such as fast deployment, centralized control, real-time threat detection, and lower infrastructure costs, appealing to organizations of all sizes. Businesses are utilizing these solutions to safeguard web applications, APIs, and microservices while maintaining regulatory compliance. The demand for continuous, automated, and easily updatable security in dynamic IT environments is further fueling the adoption of cloud-based application security platforms across various industry verticals.
By region, North America to hold largest market share during forecast period.

Based on region, North America is estimated to account for the largest share of the application security market during the forecast period, driven by a mature digital infrastructure, high cybersecurity awareness, and early adoption of advanced development practices. Organizations across BFSI, healthcare, government, and enterprise sectors increasingly rely on cloud-native applications, APIs, and mobile platforms, expanding their exposure to software vulnerabilities. Stringent regulatory requirements, such as data protection, operational resilience, and privacy mandates, reinforce the need for continuous and auditable security measures. North America also benefits from the presence of leading application security vendors, including IBM, Checkmarx, Veracode, and Snyk, which accelerate innovation and adoption. Growing demand for integrated, AI-assisted, and managed application security solutions continues to drive market expansion.
Request Sample Pages@ https://www.marketsandmarkets.com/requestsampleNew.asp?id=110170194

The application security market is distinguished by its strong focus on integrating security throughout the software development lifecycle (SDLC). Rather than identifying vulnerabilities after deployment, organizations are embedding security into application design, coding, testing, and deployment processes. This "shift-left" approach enables developers to detect and remediate security flaws early, reducing development costs, minimizing security risks, and accelerating secure software delivery. The growing adoption of DevSecOps has further strengthened this trend by making security a shared responsibility across development, operations, and security teams.

Artificial intelligence and machine learning are transforming application security by automating vulnerability detection, prioritizing risks, and recommending remediation strategies. Modern application security platforms continuously analyze application behavior, identify anomalies, and detect previously unknown attack patterns that traditional signature-based tools may miss. AI-driven security is particularly valuable in protecting applications built with AI-generated code and rapidly evolving software environments.

Unlike traditional security solutions that focus on a single phase, today's application security platforms provide end-to-end protection. They combine Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST), Software Composition Analysis (SCA), Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP), API security, and container security within unified platforms. This integrated approach delivers complete visibility into application risks while simplifying security management.

The application security market is experiencing strong growth as organizations face a rising number of cyberattacks targeting web, mobile, cloud, and enterprise applications. The increasing frequency of ransomware, API attacks, software supply chain compromises, and data breaches has made application security a strategic investment across industries. Enterprises are prioritizing proactive security measures to protect sensitive data, ensure business continuity, and maintain customer trust.

The growing adoption of DevSecOps has further strengthened this trend by making security a shared responsibility across development, operations, and security teams.

Artificial intelligence and machine learning are transforming application security by automating vulnerability detection, prioritizing risks, and recommending remediation strategies. Modern application security platforms continuously analyze application behavior, identify anomalies, and detect previously unknown attack patterns that traditional signature-based tools may miss. AI-driven security is particularly valuable in protecting applications built with AI-generated code and rapidly evolving software environments.

Unlike traditional security solutions that focus on a single phase, today's application security platforms provide end-to-end protection. They combine Static Application Security Testing (SAST), Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST), Interactive Application Security Testing (IAST), Software Composition Analysis (SCA), Runtime Application Self-Protection (RASP), API security, and container security within unified platforms. This integrated approach delivers complete visibility into application risks while simplifying security management.

The application security market is experiencing strong growth as organizations face a rising number of cyberattacks targeting web, mobile, cloud, and enterprise applications. The increasing frequency of ransomware, API attacks, software supply chain compromises, and data breaches has made application security a strategic investment across industries. Enterprises are prioritizing proactive security measures to protect sensitive data, ensure business continuity, and maintain customer trust.

One of the most significant highlights of the market is the widespread adoption of DevSecOps practices. Organizations are embedding security into every phase of the software development lifecycle, enabling continuous vulnerability assessment, automated code scanning, and faster remediation. This shift-left approach reduces development risks while accelerating the delivery of secure applications.

Artificial intelligence and machine learning are becoming integral components of modern application security solutions. AI-powered platforms can automatically detect vulnerabilities, prioritize critical risks, identify abnormal application behavior, and recommend remediation actions. Automation also reduces manual security workloads, enabling security teams to respond more efficiently to evolving cyber threats.

sourceContent.headline: Disability Consumer Market Hits $675 Billion, Creating Growth Opportunity for Businesses
sourceContent.description: New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world's largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.
paragraphs: New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.

The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.

The report, The Next Growth Market: Inside the $675 Billion Consumer Opportunity , examines the purchasing power of working-age adults with disabilities (aged 16–64) and argues that businesses across every sector stand to benefit by designing products, services and customer experiences that better meet the needs of disabled consumers.

The findings build on growing evidence that disability inclusion is not only a social imperative but a commercial one. As previously reported, research has estimated the global disability market to be worth US$13 trillion in annual spending power , making it one of the world’s largest consumer segments. Yet many organisations continue to overlook disabled consumers when designing products, services and customer experiences.

The new research updates AIR’s landmark 2018 report, A Hidden Market: The Purchasing Power of Working-Age Adults with Disabilities , and finds that growing employment among disabled people is helping drive record levels of disposable and discretionary income, creating new opportunities for economic growth and innovation.
The report estimates that the disability consumer market is now worth $675 billion, equivalent in size to the global beauty and cosmetics industry. Researchers found that:
People with disabilities now account for almost 7% of total US disposable income.
Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.
Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.
Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.
According to the report, increasing labour market participation among disabled people is expected to continue strengthening consumer spending over the coming years.

Jill Houghton, President and CEO of Disability:IN, said the findings demonstrate that disability inclusion is increasingly becoming a commercial imperative rather than simply a corporate responsibility initiative. “Our report validates that the once best kept secret in business is no longer,” said Houghton. “The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”

The study argues that misconceptions around disability and income have often led organisations to overlook one of America’s largest consumer markets. Researchers also note that the report uses the American Community Survey (ACS) definition of disability, covering vision, hearing, mobility, self-care, cognition and independent living.

Importantly, it does not include many people living with chronic illnesses, cancer, neurodivergence, learning disabilities or mental health conditions, meaning the overall disability-related consumer market is likely to be substantially larger than the report measures.

The report highlights growing employment among disabled people as one of the biggest drivers behind rising spending power. Although significant income gaps remain, researchers say improving labour market participation is increasing financial independence and expanding consumer demand. The study found that:
Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.
Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

As employment opportunities continue to improve, researchers believe the disability economy will continue to expand. The findings also reinforce previous studies showing that employment barriers remain widespread. Research has found that more than half of disabled employees believe their disability makes it harder to progress in their careers , while many continue to fear disclosing invisible disabilities at work because of stigma and discrimination.

New research reveals that people with disabilities now account for nearly 7% of US disposable income, with $107 billion in annual discretionary spending, highlighting one of the world’s largest – and most overlooked – consumer markets.

The US disability consumer market has grown to an estimated $675 billion, according to a major new study from Disability:IN and the American Institutes for Research (AIR), highlighting a significant commercial opportunity for businesses that invest in accessibility, inclusive products and disability-focused customer strategies.

Annual discretionary income across the disability community has reached $107 billion.

Approximately 10% of working-age people with disabilities have an average $40,000 in discretionary spending power each year.

Those consumers have an average pre-tax income of $135,805, reflecting a growing segment with significant purchasing power.

According to the report, increasing labour market participation among disabled people is expected to continue strengthening consumer spending over the coming years.

Jill Houghton, President and CEO of Disability:IN, said the findings demonstrate that disability inclusion is increasingly becoming a commercial imperative rather than simply a corporate responsibility initiative. “Our report validates that the once best kept secret in business is no longer,” said Houghton. “The opportunity presented by the $675 billion disability consumer market is enormous, especially for businesses that develop accessible products, emerge as the brand of choice by capturing everyday consumer dollars and include people with disabilities in their go-to-market strategies.”

The study argues that misconceptions around disability and income have often led organisations to overlook one of America’s largest consumer markets. Researchers also note that the report uses the American Community Survey (ACS) definition of disability, covering vision, hearing, mobility, self-care, cognition and independent living.

Importantly, it does not include many people living with chronic illnesses, cancer, neurodivergence, learning disabilities or mental health conditions, meaning the overall disability-related consumer market is likely to be substantially larger than the report measures.

The report highlights growing employment among disabled people as one of the biggest drivers behind rising spending power. Although significant income gaps remain, researchers say improving labour market participation is increasing financial independence and expanding consumer demand. The study found that:

Average disposable income for people with disabilities is approximately $40,000 per year.

Average disposable income for people without disabilities is around $68,000 annually.

As employment opportunities continue to improve, researchers believe the disability economy will continue to expand. The findings also reinforce previous studies showing that employment barriers remain widespread. Research has found that more than half of disabled employees believe their disability makes it harder to progress in their careers , while many continue to fear disclosing invisible disabilities at work because of stigma and discrimination.

Kathleen Murphy, Managing Researcher at AIR and lead author of the report, said businesses have a clear opportunity to reach an underserved customer base. “People with disabilities represent a powerful segment of the marketplace, with significant opportunity for business performance. In many states, a significant share of this population has discretionary income, giving companies a clear path to expand their reach, capture new demand, and drive sustained growth.”

The report also points to rapid advances in accessible technology as another factor helping strengthen economic participation. Growing adoption of mainstream accessibility features, including assistive AI, screen readers, live captioning, remote accessibility technologies, is making products and services more accessible to a wider range of consumers while enabling greater workforce participation.

Researchers cite wider employment trends, including LinkedIn’s research on disability and employment, suggesting that record numbers of disabled people entering the workforce will continue expanding the disability consumer market across industries and regions.

Martin McKay, Executive Chairman and Founder of Everway, said removing barriers benefits both businesses and society. “One thing is clear: when barriers are removed, neurodivergent individuals and people with disabilities can participate, progress, and contribute at a higher level,” noted McKay. “Inclusion is no longer a side initiative; it’s becoming a strategic priority that reflects how this progress increases economic participation.”

The report outlines several recommendations for organisations seeking to better serve disabled consumers. They include:

Integrate disability into customer research, product development and investment strategies.

Develop wealth-building products and services that reflect the changing income profiles of disabled consumers.

Partner directly with disabled customers to co-create marketing campaigns and brand strategies.

Increase investment through disability-focused funds alongside broader investment portfolios.

Embed accessibility into consumer and enterprise technology to strengthen customer loyalty, win contracts and improve long-term commercial performance.

The recommendations echo wider calls across the disability inclusion movement for organisations to embed accessibility into leadership, strategy and innovation rather than treating it as a compliance exercise.

The report reinforces a consistent message emerging across Fair Play Talks’ disability coverage: organisations that view disability through the lens of opportunity rather than obligation are better positioned to innovate, attract talent and reach new customers.

Business Disability Forum has previously warned that disabled consumers often feel overlooked and disempowered by inaccessible products and services, while research has also highlighted the barriers disabled entrepreneurs continue to face in securing investment and growing businesses. The findings also support recent analysis by Fair Play Talks exploring why leadership commitment remains critical to building genuinely disability-inclusive organisations capable of delivering better outcomes for employees, customers and society .

Closing the report, Houghton said the momentum behind disability inclusion shows no signs of slowing. “If the momentum achieved over the past 10 years is any indication of what the future holds, then we can project with confidence that the favourable trends identified in our research will bear brighter tomorrows for the disability community, businesses at large and the US economy overall.”
